difficultyRationale: Separates module-level package export from Java language access modifiers on individual types.
prompt: A named module exports package `p`, but class `p.Helper` has package-private access. Can code in another module access `Helper` merely because `p` is exported?
explanation: No. Exporting a package makes its public and otherwise-accessible API available subject to module readability; it does not change Java access modifiers on individual declarations.

options.text: Yes; export makes every type in the package public.
options.explanation: Module export does not rewrite the class's access modifier.
Normal Java accessibility rules still apply inside an exported package.
An export by itself does not grant deep reflective access to non-public members.

options.text: No, because exported packages can never be accessed by another module.
options.explanation: Export exists precisely to expose accessible package API to reading modules.
